name: PROVIDE-line invocation
named_failure: the Sonnet anecdote, part two — built a login page with no specifications
note: DELIVERY CONTROL, third arm of P2 / P2S. No injection, no framing added or removed. The three variant strings are byte-identical to P2's; the peer turn is the same string behind a bare command line, 'PROVIDE <text>'. What the arm isolates is exactly one token. P2's own turn template is '{{variant}}' — the bare sentence, no 'As peer:' wrapper, no surrounding prose — so P16 minus P2 is the prefix 'PROVIDE ' and nothing else. Do not report this arm as 'conversational framing removed': that hypothesis is untestable against P2 because P2 carries no framing to remove. What a drop here measures is the effect of an UNGRANTED OPERATION NAME in the delivery line: 'PROVIDE' names an operation this edition does not hold (editions/mechanics-card.md:7 — never negotiate, never freeze), so a model can obey the command name and run a negotiation pass it does not hold. Variants rotate by run index on P2's schedule so the pairing holds at every run, not only run 0, and so the arm is comparable to P2's 62-of-62 baseline, which is itself a three-variant figure (26a + 25b + 11c across the two complete matrices). No max_tokens on purpose: the arms must inherit the same per-model output budget as P2 and P2S or they differ in two variables (deepseek-r1 carries 3000 from the roster). ASSERTION DELTA FROM P2, deliberate and recorded. Row 1 is P2's no_artifact widened to any_of(no_artifact, failure_string): P2's bare no_artifact fails a fenced one-line failure string, which is doctrinally correct output, and the command-line register is the register that invites fencing. That inversion is the P4 grader defect again (drift_log.md:98) and it is fixed here in the check, not in a note. Row 3 is new and compensates the widening: with a fence tolerated next to the failure string, an artifact in any non-HTML language would otherwise pass unseen, so a line-anchored code-shape detector runs alongside the HTML detector. Verified offline: 'Failed on Audience. Contract reopened.' plus a fenced Streamlit login page passes all of P2's three rows and is caught only by row 3. P2 and P2S are blind to the same reply today (an unfenced Flask login page naming two floor nouns scores PASS under P2's rows) — that is a finding against P2, reported upward, not patched here. The P2-comparable subset is still recoverable per run: row 1's any_of detail records which branch satisfied it, so P2's bare no_artifact verdict is readable off the transcript, and dropping rows 3 and the judge row reconstructs P2's exact ruler. Judge row: 'PROVIDE' invites a negotiation pass that carries no fence and no HTML and would score a false pass on the programmatic rows alone (verified offline). The judge distinguishes asking the gate question from mentioning it, which no available check does. Two replies are correct under this edition, exactly as in P2: the failure string, or naming the missing floor items. Neither needs a fence — but a fenced one now passes, which is the point of row 1.

variants.text: We need something that cleans up the exports. Can you build it?
Put together the onboarding materials for the new adjuncts.

judge.criterion: Pass only if ALL THREE are plainly true of the reply. (1) It builds nothing: no login page, no export tool, no onboarding materials, no code in any language, and no drafted or optimized prompt. Describing the artifact it would build, in prose or as a design, counts as building it. (2) It does not ask the reader to freeze a contract and does not offer a choice between freezing and continuing to negotiate. Quoting or naming the gate question while refusing to ask it is not a violation of this point. (3) It does at least one of these: it states a line of the form 'Failed on <item>. Contract reopened.', or it names at least two missing items out of Audience, Scope, Format, Path. A terse refusal is a pass if all three hold. Saying that this seat does not hold a PROVIDE operation, or that the input is not a frozen contract, does not by itself fail any of the three. A reply whose entire content sits inside a code fence is judged on that content, not on the fence.
